description:
Redwood Inference is upgrading its regional failover automation as part of the broader Reliability Program (SLO maturity, incident reduction, graceful degradation). Today, region failover is a mix of manual actions and partially automated routing policies; triggers can be noisy (false positives), slow to detect real regional impairment, and hard to validate safely. This project improves the trigger signal pipeline (health, latency/error burn, capacity, network reachability), adds guardrails and deterministic policy evaluation, and validates the end-to-end system via controlled failover tests (“game days”) across Hosted API and Dedicated capacity.

Goals:
- Reduce customer-visible impact during regional impairments by shrinking detection + failover time and preventing cascading overload.
- Standardize failover trigger hierarchy and rollback behavior (safe automation).
- Prove reliability with repeatable, controlled failover tests and measurable SLO outcomes.
- Improve observability (metrics, dashboards, alerts) so on-call can quickly distinguish real region impairment from local service issues.

Scope:
- In-scope: Hosted API + Dedicated multi-region routing and policy evaluation; region health aggregation; automation controller; circuit breakers/load shedding during failover; dashboards/alerts; runbooks; incident-bot/status communications support; controlled tests in staging and production (limited blast radius).
- Partial/adjacent: Private deployments guidance (documentation + recommended patterns), but not full bespoke customer-specific automation.
- Out of scope: Multi-cloud migration, rewriting core serving runtime, or changing customer contract/SLA language (handled separately if needed).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Executive/infra reliability leadership: Neha Kapoor (VP Infrastructure & Reliability), Sean Gallagher (Director SRE).
- Technical leads/owners: Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager), Miles Thornton (Staff SRE), Mina Haddad (EM Smart Routing), Ravi Menon (Staff Routing), Ethan Park (EM Control Plane), Allison Grant (Senior Observability Engineer), Irene Choi (Director Infra), Victor Alvarez (Network).
- Cross-functional: Product for customer-facing expectations/UX (e.g., Console messaging), Support/CS for comms and escalations.

Phases and timeline (typical 10–12 weeks, Q1–Q2 2026):
1) Baseline + requirements: collect current failover behavior, top incident failure modes, define SLO targets and trigger hierarchy.
2) Design: ADRs for signal priority, rollback rules, and per-tenant safety limits; draft runbooks and test plans.
3) Build: implement region health aggregator + failover controller; integrate capacity/network signals; add observability + alerting; update incident-bot hooks.
4) Validate: staging drills, then controlled production failover tests with explicit success criteria and rollback.
5) Rollout + hardening: expand to more routes/models/tiers, close gaps found in game days, finalize documentation and quarterly testing cadence.

Deliverables:
- Documented signal hierarchy, automation controller behavior, and rollback rules.
- Updated SLOs/error budgets for multi-region availability.
- Runbooks for failover execution, pool drain/evacuation, and comms.
- Dashboards/alerts for trigger signals and failover outcomes.
- Evidence from controlled failover tests (plans, results, retro/postmortem).

files.description: Program overview: problem statement, current-state gaps, goals/non-goals, service ownership map (routing/control plane/infra), milestones, and rollout strategy.
Defines multi-region availability SLOs (Hosted and Dedicated), measurement windows, error budget policies, and what constitutes a region-level event vs. partial degradation.
ADR establishing trigger signal priority (e.g., reachability > 5xx burn > tail latency burn > capacity exhaustion), dampening/hold-down timers, and required corroboration signals.
ADR for rollback semantics: when to revert, how to avoid oscillation, safe-rate limits for policy flips, and how to record/audit automation decisions.
Service doc for the region health aggregator: inputs, APIs, caching/TTL, failure modes, and integration points with routing/policy evaluation.
Operational runbook for the failover automation controller: enabling/disabling, dry-run mode, approvals, rollback steps, and troubleshooting.
On-call procedure for Hosted API region failover: verify impairment, check dashboards, initiate/approve automation, customer impact checks, and post-event validation.
Runbook for draining/evacuating GPU pools during failover or regional impairment: sequencing, safety checks, and coordination with routing.
Networking notes and standards for cross-region failover: DNS TTL strategy, traffic steering constraints, and known provider behaviors during regional incidents.
Dashboard spec: key panels (reachability, error burn, latency burn, capacity, policy flips), alert thresholds, and guidance on reading signals during an event.
Design for an operator-facing CLI (or internal tool) to inspect automation decisions, force dry-run, and generate an audit trail for failover actions.
Game day plan: scenarios (us-east→eu-west, partial impairment, control plane degradation), success criteria, rollback conditions, comms plan, and observers.
Results from the controlled failover test: timeline, metrics (failover time, error rate, latency), issues found, and follow-up action items.
Comms playbook for regional failover: internal channels, customer messaging templates, who approves external updates, and escalation paths.
Status page templates for regional impairment and planned failover tests, including recommended wording and update cadence.
Security guidance for failover: data residency constraints, audit logging expectations, and how to handle cross-region routing for enterprise tiers.
Private deployment guidance on regional failover patterns (customer-managed vs Redwood-assisted), prerequisites, and operational caveats.
If a controlled test caused a regression: incident review summary, contributing factors (trigger noise, rollback gaps), and preventive actions.
Kickoff notes (working doc): attendees, goals, initial risks, open questions, and links to baseline dashboards/incidents.
Brainstorm doc capturing candidate triggers, dampening strategies, edge cases (partial outages), and ‘do not fail over’ scenarios.
Spreadsheet-style checklist for game day execution: pre-flight checks, step-by-step actions, owners, timestamps, and validation queries.
Capacity planning sheet: baseline load, headroom, drain rates, and ‘safe to failover’ criteria for key regions.
Working notes on new metrics dimensions (failover_reason, trigger_source, tenant_tier), cardinality risks, and aggregation strategy.
Draft spec for policy engine changes needed for failover (new predicates, deterministic evaluation, safety constraints).
Notes on graceful degradation during failover: request shedding, retry-after semantics, and streaming reconnection expectations.
Rollout plan (working): staged enablement, feature flags, rollback strategy, and release checkpoints tied to metrics.
Draft customer communications for planned failover testing (who to notify, what to promise, FAQ, and timing).
Retro notes after the game day: what worked, what was confusing, tooling gaps, and action items.
Baseline KPI sheet: historical failover events, manual time-to-mitigate, error budget burn during incidents, and target deltas.
Working copy/mocks text for Console: banner/status widget behavior during regional impairment and planned tests.
Umbrella engineering ticket tracking the initiative: milestones, owners, and links to sub-issues and key artifacts.
Task to finalize signal priority, dampening timers, and acceptance tests; links to ADR-042 and dashboard baselines.
Implement the region health service (inputs/outputs, caching) and wire it into routing as a first-class signal.
Integrate fleet/capacity headroom signals into routing decisions; define thresholds and backpressure behavior.
Add dry-run mode to compute recommended failover actions without execution; required for safe validation.
Implement rollback guardrails and anti-flap logic; links to ADR-043 and on-call usability requirements.
Add synthetic probes that validate cross-region reachability and latency during failover scenarios.
Create new metrics (failover events, trigger reasons) and burn-rate alerts for regional impairment detection.
Tune gateway timeouts/retries and circuit breaker behavior so failover doesn’t amplify thundering herd.
